department: School of Engineering — Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

deadline.value: Regular Fall 2027-28 application deadline is omitted from the Mechanical Engineering 2027-28 catalog page (unlike other HKUST School of Engineering PhD catalog pages which list June 1, 2027 non-local rolling); FYTGS Admissions Timeline lists applications opening September 1, 2026, HKPFS deadline December 1, 2026, and individual program deadlines December 2026 onwards.
deadline.quote: The application deadline for individual program vary, please visit here ("Application" tab of individual program page) for details | December 2026 onwards | 1 December 2026 (11:59pm, GMT+8)

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for mechanical and aerospace engineering (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering admission and 2027-28 catalog pages do not state a pre-application supervisor contact requirement.

funding.value: Full-time PhD students are eligible for HKUST Postgraduate Studentships (HK$229,620/yr, ~US$29,420/yr for up to 4 years), RedBird PhD Award, and HKPFS.
funding.quote: Postgraduate Studentship (PGS) | HK$229,620 per year (~US$29,420/ year) | Up to 4 years for full-time PhD students

entry_route.value: Admits bachelor's holders with outstanding performance (4-year full-time PhD) and research master's holders (3-year full-time PhD).
entry_route.quote: Full-time: 3 years (with a relevant research master’s degree), 4 years (without a relevant research master’s degree) | Applicants seeking admissions to a doctoral degree program should have obtained a bachelor’s degree with a proven record of outstanding performance from a recognized institution

also.quote: Qualified applicants may be admitted directly to the PhD program.

notes: Covers Solid Mechanics & Dynamics, Materials Technology, Energy/Thermalfluids & Environment, Design & Manufacturing Automation, MEMS, and Aerospace Engineering, with optional Energy Technology, Nanotechnology, and Scientific Computation concentrations.
